title: TypeScript Strict Discipline
description: Type laundering — places where `any` and unchecked casts hide bugs.

rules.message: Double cast `as unknown as X` bypasses type system entirely — almost always a smell.
rules.remediation: Define proper types, use type guard, or fix the source type. Double cast is last resort.

rules.message: Non-null assertion on array access (`arr[i]!`) silently crashes on out-of-bounds.
rules.remediation: Use length check: `arr[i] ?? fallback` or `if (arr.length > i) arr[i]`.

rules.message: Function parameter typed `any` — caller can pass anything, type errors invisible.
rules.remediation: Type the parameter properly or use `unknown` and validate. `any` only for true escape hatch.

rules.message: Exported function without explicit return type — TS infers but consumers see `any` on errors.
rules.remediation: Add `: ReturnType` after the parameter list for exported functions.

rules.message: String literal status — invites typos. Consider a union type or const enum.
